titleEn: Rice Balls, Sitting on the Porch!

pages.text: "Wow, rice balls!" Grandma set a plate on the porch. Yuki grabbed one. "I'll eat quickly and go to the stream!"
Yuki ran around the porch with the rice ball in hand. "I can eat it while running!" Yuki grinned. Grandma watched from the porch's edge.
Then a foot caught on the threshold. The rice ball fell, scattering grains. Brown dog Momo hurried over.
Momo licked up the scattered rice. Only half a ball remained in Yuki's hand. "My rice ball..." Yuki curled their fingers.
Grandma patted a porch board. "Sit here. A summer porch cools your bottom." She sang, "Rice Balls, Sitting on the Porch!"
Yuki sat with their bottom firmly on the board. It really was cool. Grandma put a fresh rice ball in their hand. "Oh? My bottom seems to stick here!"
Even with Momo waiting beside them, tail waving, Yuki stayed seated. Holding with both hands, Yuki ate without dropping a grain. With the last bite, Yuki said, "Rice Balls, Sitting on the Porch!"
The plate was empty! "I ate it all!" Yuki raised both hands. Not one grain lay on the boards.

The next day, Yuki sat as soon as the plate arrived and fixed the scarf knot. Three fingers rose. "One, bottom on the cool porch! Two, hold with both hands and chew! Three, sit until the plate is empty!"

Yuki leaned toward Grandma. She touched cheeks and stroked their back. Sitting to eat kept rice from spilling and the tummy comfortable. "Grandma, let's go to the stream! Rice Balls, Sitting on the Porch!"
